subject: C33
required_fixes: R1 — crates/desktop-core/src/authority.rs:2363, crates/desktop-core/src/scanning.rs:218 and packages/desktop-contracts/src/client.ts:2030: a case result copies the scan's sanitized identifier without validating it, while isCaseResult requires a nonempty scanId. The pinned SDK's ScanResponseSchema accepts empty strings; stripping control characters can also produce an empty identifier. A case-bound scan with such a response therefore creates a ShellSnapshot that the production parser rejects. library.rs:351 retains this Runtime result on reload, so the problem persists after restart. Align native result construction, stored-result validation and the renderer contract without inventing identifiers. Acceptance: empty and control-only service scan IDs through the production scan/authority path leave all shell observations parser-valid before and after restart, with honest result presentation and no replay.

R2 — crates/desktop-core/src/authority.rs:2377, authority/library_domain.rs:718 and library.rs:657: recording a case result mutates the library without enforcing LIBRARY_BYTES, and store writes it without a size check. A valid library near 256 KiB can consequently be replaced with a file that from_cases rejects on restart, making all its cases unavailable and setting the file aside as unreadable. An in-memory serialized example with three valid Runtime cases grows from 262143 to 262201 bytes after one ordinary result. Preserve the library's storage invariant when adding result metadata and prevent invalid replacements. Acceptance: an authority-level near-limit case scan, save and restart preserve every authored case and a readable library; any result-storage limitation is reported honestly, and every successful write is accepted by the production loader.

R3 — apps/desktop/src/v2/workbench/test-cases.tsx:130 and :147: Export dispatches exportCases but the screen never reads library.export. Unlike the retained LibraryView at :387, it silently ignores saving, saved, cancelled and failed outcomes, including native save failures, and drops the explanation that exported prompts/responses are plaintext. Restore the observed export lifecycle and content disclosure in the v2 presentation. Acceptance: production-client component tests push all four ExportState values and assert the corresponding accessible status/error and saved filename; native export success, cancellation and failure produce the matching visible outcome.
